title: Reacting to News and Social Problems

sections.title: Fact first, reaction second
sections.content: Lessons 1 to 4 gave you four ways to react: verbs that work like *gustar* (*me preocupa que*), verbs with the person as subject (*lamento que*), exclamations (*¡Qué pena que!*) and *el hecho de que*. When you talk about news or a social problem you usually need both parts: first the fact, in the indicative, and then your reaction, in the subjunctive. You know *gustar* from A1 Unit 22 and *molestar* from A2 Unit 27.

sections.title: Fact + reaction
rows: Hay mucho desempleo y me preocupa que no haya más ayuda.
There is a lot of unemployment and it worries me that there is no more help.
La pobreza sigue creciendo. Lamento que nadie haga nada.
Poverty keeps growing. I'm sorry that nobody does anything.
¡Qué pena que tantas personas no tengan trabajo!
What a shame that so many people don't have a job!
El hecho de que haya tanta desigualdad nos preocupa.
The fact that there is so much inequality worries us.

items.spanish: Me preocupa que la contaminación afecte la salud de los niños.
items.english: It worries me that pollution affects children's health.

items.spanish: Es una pena que muchos jóvenes no encuentren trabajo.
items.english: It's a pity that many young people can't find work.

items.spanish: Nos molesta que los precios suban cada mes.
items.english: It bothers us that prices go up every month.

items.spanish: ¡Qué injusto que unos tengan tanto y otros tan poco!
items.english: How unfair that some have so much and others so little!

sections.content: The fact is in the indicative because you are telling it (*Hay mucho desempleo*); your reaction takes the subjunctive. If you name the problem with a noun, you need no *que*: *Me preocupa la contaminación*, or with a plural noun, *Me preocupan los precios*.
